description: We are a multi-disciplinary engineering and software development team building next-generation mission design tools. For the Space Mission Design Game challenge, we developed O2S: Mission Architect—a high-performance, interactive aerospace trade-off engine that bridges real-world orbital mechanics (multi-stage Tsiolkovsky $\Delta v$ budgets, planetary transfer orbits, and inverse-square solar power scaling) with an intuitive game loop.
summary: Project Orpheus is a high-fidelity mission architecture simulator designed to bridge the gap between orbital physics and financial reality. Many conceptual simulators ignore the strict constraints of mass, power, and budget. Orpheus enforces them. Powered by real-world NASA and space agency data, our physics engine dynamically calculates the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation against launch vehicle capabilities and payload masses. If a mission design lacks the Delta-V to reach its target, or if its power systems fail in deep space (e.g., solar arrays at Jupiter), the engine scrubs the launch. Our UI provides real-time telemetry, constraint tracking, and 2D orbital trajectory visualization, forcing users to engineer mathematically and financially viable mission profiles, such as our showcased "Oceanus" Europa flyby. Project Orpheus proves that true aerospace innovation happens where orbital mechanics and hard constraints meet.
details: Project Orpheus is an interactive mission architecture dashboard that simulates the physical and financial constraints of interplanetary spaceflight. It calculates real-time Delta-V requirements using the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, dynamically adjusting for payload mass variations (e.g., standard solar arrays vs. heavy nuclear RTGs). We utilized Python and Streamlit for the backend logic and UI, integrating Three.js for WebGL orbital trajectory mapping. The primary benefit is bridging the gap between theoretical orbital mechanics and real-world mission budgets. By forcing users to balance launch vehicle costs against physical mass limits and environmental factors (like Jupiter's solar power blackouts), Orpheus provides a mathematically rigorous look at aerospace engineering tradeoffs.
